source_text:
Τούτου
τοῦ ῥητοῦ, ὡς χρησίμου μνημονεύωμεν, ὅταν ὁ Θεὸς παθεῖν τι ἡμᾶς κρίνῃ, τέκνον
ἀποβαλεῖν, ἀρχὴν ἀπολέσαι, νοσῆσαι κατὰ τὸ σῶμα. ὅ τι δήποτε τούτων ὑποστῆναι·
οὐδὲν τούτων οἷόν τε παθεῖν ἡμᾶς, μὴ κρίνοντος τοῦ Θεοῦ. Ἐπεὶ οὖν οὐδὲν τούτων
γίνεται χωρὶς κρίματος τοῦ Θεοῦ, λέγεται πρὸς τὸν παθόντα· «Μὴ ἀποποιοῦ μου τὸ
κρῖμα·» τουτέστι, Μὴ ἀπαρνοῦ ὅπερ ἔκρινα περὶ σοῦ· τὸν παρόντα λέγει
χρηματισμόν. Οἴει δέ με ἄλλως σοι κεχρηματικέναι, ἢ ἵνα ἀναφανῇς δίκαιος;
Ἀπολογοῦμαί σοι· δίκαιος ἦς, ἀλλ' οὐκ ἦς φανερός· ὑπομονὴν εἶχες· ἔδει με ἀφορμὴν
παρασχεῖν τοῦ λάμψαι σου τὴν ὑπομονήν· εἶχες ἀνδρείαν· ἀλλ' ἐκρύπτετο ἐν σοί· οἱ
συμβεβηκότες πόνοι ἔδειξάν σου τὴν ἀνδρείαν. Τούτων μνημονεύωμεν ἐν τοῖς τῶν
περιστάσεων καιροῖς, καὶ δόξω 12.1048 μεν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀκούειν παρόντος καὶ λέγοντος
ἡμῖν· «Οἴει δέ με ἄλλως σοι κεχρηματικέναι,» τουτέστι τὸν πειρασμὸν συγχωρῆσαι, ἢ
ἵνα τοῖς ἀγνοοῦσι δήλη ἡ σὴ δικαιοσύνη ᾖ; Ἀνάλαβε δὴ ὕψος. Ἔστι δὲ καὶ οὕτω
νοῆσαι τοὺς στίχους· Νενίκηκας τὸν πειραστήν· ἀνάλαβέ σου τὸ ὕψος· ἀνάλαβέ σου
τὴν δύναμιν· στεφάνωσαι· ἔνδυσαι εὐπρέπειαν. Ὁ ὑβριστὴς ἐστρατεύσατο κατὰ σοῦ·
σὺ δὲ τὸν ὑπερήφανον ἐταπείνωσας, καὶ μακρὰν μετ' αἰσχύνης ἀπέστρεψας μετὰ τῆς
αὐτοῦ φάλαγγος. ΚΕΦ. ΜΑʹ. Παίξῃ δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ ὥσπερ ὀρνέῳ; ἢ δήσεις αὐτὸν ὥσπερ
στρουθίον παιδίῳ;
thought_title: God's words to Job as a gift after victory
orientation: Origen is expounding God's address to Job after his trials, explaining that every suffering comes by God's judgment and that God's questions to Job are meant to reveal his hidden virtues.
pass_a_gloss: Let us remember this saying as useful, whenever God judges us to suffer something, to lose a child, to lose a rule, to be sick in the body. Whatever of these things we undergo; none of these things is it possible for us to suffer, if God does not judge it. Since therefore none of these things happens without the judgment of God, it is said to the one who has suffered: "Do not reject my judgment"; that is, Do not deny what I judged concerning you; he means the present oracle. Do you think that I have dealt with you otherwise, than in order that you may be revealed as righteous? I make my defense to you; you were righteous, but you were not manifest; you had endurance; it was necessary for me to provide an occasion for your endurance to shine; you had courage; but it was hidden in you; the pains that befell you showed your courage. Let us remember these things in the times of adversities, and we shall seem to hear God present and saying to us: "Do you think that I have dealt with you otherwise," that is, to have permitted the trial, than in order that your righteousness may be clear to those who do not know? Take up then height. And it is also possible to understand the verses thus: You have conquered the tempter; take up your height; take up your power; be crowned; clothe yourself with splendor. The insolent one marched against you; but you humbled the arrogant one, and you turned him back far off with shame together with his phalanx. CHAPTER 41. Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you bind him as a sparrow for a child?

choices.why: The glossary requires 'judgment' for κρῖμα, and the verb means to push away or reject; this keeps the command's force.
rejected: Do not cast off my verdict

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'endurance' for Job's chief virtue.
The word denotes a divine response or communication; 'oracle' preserves the sense of God's present address to Job.
The imperative is direct and the particle δή adds urgency; 'height' is kept literal to preserve the spatial metaphor of exaltation.
rejected: Take up then your high estate

choices.why: The glossary uses 'trial' for πειρασμός, so the agent noun is rendered 'tempter' to match the same root and the brief's identification of Satan.

bible_refs.note: Παίξῃ δὲ ἐν αὐτῷ ὥσπερ ὀρνέῳ; ἢ δήσεις αὐτὸν ὥσπερ στρουθίον παιδίῳ;

pass_b_english: Let us remember this saying as useful whenever God judges that we should suffer something: to lose a child, to lose a position, to fall ill in body, or to undergo anything whatever of this kind. None of these things can happen to us unless God judges it. Since, then, none of these things occurs without God's judgment, the one who suffers is told, “Do not reject my judgment” (Job 40:8). That is, do not deny what I have judged concerning you; he means the present oracle. God says to him, “Do you think I have dealt with you for any other reason than that you might be revealed as righteous? I make my defense to you: you were righteous, but you were not seen to be so. You had endurance, but I needed to provide an occasion for your endurance to shine. You had courage, but it was hidden within you; the pains that befell you displayed your courage.”

Let us remember these things in times of adversity, and we will seem to hear God present and saying to us, “Do you think I have dealt with you for any other reason”—that is, permitted the trial—“than that your righteousness might be clear to those who do not know it? Take up your height.”

The verses can also be understood this way: You have conquered the tempter; take up your height. Take up your power. Be crowned. Clothe yourself in splendor. The arrogant one marched against you, but you humbled the proud one and turned him back far off in shame with his whole host.
Chapter 41. Will you play with him as with a bird, or bind him as a sparrow for a child? (Job 41:5)

polish.changed: Clarified that God is the speaker of the quoted words to Job by adding 'God says to him,' and kept the quotation marks closed through the end of God's speech so the reader can follow who is speaking.

problems.why: God's words in first person without clear attribution markers.

problems.why: 'Take up then height' is not idiomatic English; likely a literal gloss of a Greek phrase.
problems.fix: Render as 'Take up your height' or 'Assume your stature,' with a note.

edits.old: God says to him, “Do you think I have spoken to you for any other reason than that you might be revealed as righteous?
edits.new: God says to him, “Do you think I have dealt with you for any other reason than that you might be revealed as righteous?

fixed: Speaker attribution: The English already introduces the first-person speech with 'God says to him,' so the speaker is clear; no edit needed.
Speaker attribution: The second first-person speech is introduced by 'God present and saying to us,' so the speaker is clear; no edit needed.
Mistranslation: 'Take up then height' is a literal rendering of ἀνάλαβε δὴ ὕψος; 'Take up your height' is more idiomatic and matches the source's possessive sense.

last_rejected.why: Greek says “to forgive the trial”, not “to permit” it.
last_rejected.fix: that is, to forgive the trial
last_rejected.ruling: συγχωρέω regularly means 'allow/permit/grant'; God permitting the trial fits the context of κρίμα and suffering; 'forgive' would be contextually odd.
